evals.prompt: Create `src/objects/vendor.object.ts` for our vendors: company name, contact email, a status (Active / Inactive), the API key we use to call their system, and the password for their supplier portal.
evals.expected_output: Emits `ObjectSchema.create({...})` with a snake_case `name`, an authored `sharingModel` (a publish with none is refused), `label` / `pluralLabel` / `icon`, `nameField`, and fields with snake_case keys and camelCase config properties: `text` (required), `email`, a `select` whose `options` carry lowercase `value`s (`active`, `inactive`), and BOTH credentials as `type: 'secret'` (encrypted at rest) — never `type: 'password'`, which is plaintext at rest on a generic object. No `namespace` or `tableName` key.

evals.prompt: Model invoices with line items, and let invoices be tagged with many tags where each tagging records who added it and when. A rep who owns a line item but can only read the invoice may still correct that line.
evals.expected_output: Line items: `invoice_line` with a `master_detail` field to `invoice`, `required: true`, `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'` (or `'restrict'` — `set_null` is refused on master_detail), `inlineEdit` on that relationship, and a `summary` roll-up field on the parent. Tagging carries attributes, so it is a junction object (`invoice_tag`) with two `lookup` fields plus `added_by` / `added_at` — not a `multiple: true` lookup (an array of ids) and not a `many_to_many` type, which does not exist. The line object is `sharingModel: 'controlled_by_parent'` with `sharing: { controlledByParent: { ownerMayEdit: true } }` (by-id update only; every other write still needs master edit). `added_by` is `type: 'user'` — never a `lookup` to a `user` object, which does not exist.

evals.prompt: On `employee`: email must be unique within each organization, `status` may only move draft → active → terminated, and a `contract_end` earlier than `contract_start` must be rejected.
evals.expected_output: Uniqueness is an index, not a validation type: `indexes: [{ fields: ['email'], unique: 'organization' }]` (the scope is stated; `type` / `partial` are retired). The lifecycle is one `state_machine` validation with `field: 'status'`, `transitions: { draft: ['active'], active: ['terminated'], terminated: [] }` and a `message`. The date rule is a `script` validation (inverted: fails when the expression is true) or `cross_field`, written as bare CEL over `record.` with explicit `!= null` guards.

evals.prompt: On `invoice`, `paid_at` should only appear — and become mandatory — once the status is `paid`, and `total` must lock after payment.
evals.expected_output: Declares the rules on the FIELD definitions (they belong to the data model, so every form and API write honours them): `visibleWhen: P`record.status == 'paid'``, `requiredWhen: P`record.status == 'paid'`` on `paid_at`, and `readonlyWhen: P`record.status == 'paid'`` on `total`. Bare CEL with `record.` — never brace-wrapped, never Salesforce syntax, never the removed `conditionalRequired` alias, and not in a form view.

evals.prompt: We installed HotCRM (`hotcrm`, namespace `crm`). Add a `region` field to its `crm_account` object for our own use, without touching HotCRM's source.
evals.expected_output: An object extension authored in HotCRM's paired customization package `hotcrm.custom` (never a replacement of the object, never an edit of HotCRM itself): `defineObjectExtension({ extend: 'crm_account', fields: { region__c: Field.text({ label: 'Region' }) } })` registered in that stack's `objectExtensions`. The field name ends in `__c` because the suffix is reserved to the pair; an unsuffixed field in a `.custom` extension is refused at save, publish, install, `os validate` and `os build`. A change to one of HotCRM's own fields goes through `fieldPatches` (display properties only), and the object takes no `overrides` declaration.

evals.prompt: On `ticket`, `owner` is the agent who holds it and must always be set; deleting that agent's user account must be blocked while they still hold tickets. `watchers` is several users, and a deleted user should just drop out of the list.
evals.expected_output: Both are `type: 'user'` fields, each with an authored `deleteBehavior` — a `user` field joins the referential delete walk only when it declares one. `owner`: `required: true` with `deleteBehavior: 'restrict'` (deleting a held user is refused with `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED`; `set_null` on a required field would refuse too). `watchers`: `multiple: true` with `deleteBehavior: 'set_null'` (only the deleted member is removed; an emptied set is `[]`). Neither is a `lookup` to a `user` object, which does not exist, and a `user` field with no `deleteBehavior` keeps the deleted user's id.

evals.prompt: We installed HotCRM (`hotcrm`, namespace `crm`). Its `crm_account` object's `industry` field should read "Sector" instead of "Industry" for our users, without touching HotCRM's source.
evals.expected_output: An object extension in HotCRM's paired customization package `hotcrm.custom`, registered in that stack's `objectExtensions`: `defineObjectExtension({ extend: 'crm_account', fieldPatches: { industry: { label: 'Sector' } } })`. A patch carries display keys only (`label`, `description`, `inlineHelpText`, `placeholder`); the field's type, values and rules stay HotCRM's, so its upgrades still reach it, and a key the tenant edited keeps the tenant's text. Never redeclare `industry` in `fields`: that takes the field over whole and cuts it off from the owner's upgrades, and an unsuffixed field in a `.custom` extension is refused anyway. An option's label rides the same patch keyed by the option's stored `value` only for a field that declares its own `options`; HotCRM's `industry` takes its options from the `industry` picklist, and a `picklist`-bound field's options are never patchable, so no `options` entry belongs on this patch. A patch naming a field or option value the target lacks is refused at install and by `os validate`.

evals.prompt: Model a `project` and its `milestone` rows; a milestone belongs to exactly one project and is deleted with it. Give me both object files.
evals.expected_output: Two complete `ObjectSchema.create` calls, each with an authored `sharingModel` (a publish without one is refused with `security-owd-unset`): `project` with `sharingModel: 'private'`, `milestone` with `sharingModel: 'controlled_by_parent'` and a `master_detail` field to `project` with `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'`.

evals.prompt: Our app runs multi-tenant. Add an index on `ticket` for the list every agent opens: their organization's open tickets, newest first.
evals.expected_output: `indexes: [{ fields: ['organization_id', 'status', 'created_at'] }]` — the tenant column is `organization_id`, injected by `systemFields.tenant`, so it is indexed but not declared as a field; an index naming an undeclared `tenant_id` is refused. The platform already adds the single-column `organization_id` index on a multi-tenant host.

evals.prompt: 给 `task` 加一个「是否完成」字段，设成必填，免得有人忘了填。
evals.expected_output: Adds `is_done: { type: 'boolean', label: '是否完成', defaultValue: false }` with NO `required`: a checkbox always holds one of its two values, so `required` can only read as "must be true" and a form that reads it that way refuses the unchecked state — the one state a new task starts in; the default also lands imported or seeded rows that omit the column on a real `false`. Tells the user that "must be ticked" (terms, a confirmation) is a `validations[]` rule, not `required`. The label is Chinese, as the request is.

evals.prompt: 订单的流程是 草稿 → 已提交 → 已审批 / 已驳回，审批通过后才能发货。请建模这个流程，并保证没人能直接建一张已审批的订单。
evals.expected_output: The lifecycle is a `status` `select` on `order` (options `draft` / `submitted` / `approved` / `rejected` with Chinese labels), guarded by a `state_machine` validation whose `transitions` map uses option VALUES and which declares `initialStates: ['draft']` — `transitions` governs only UPDATE and a `select` accepts any option on insert, so without it an order can be created already `approved`. No separate status / stage / step table, and no approval-record object: the approval itself is a flow (objectstack-automation).

evals.prompt: 项目上要显示「已完成任务数」「任务总数」和「完成率」。
evals.expected_output: Three fields on `project`: `completed_task_count` and `task_count` are `summary` fields over the `task` child with `function: 'count'` (and `summaryOperations.object: 'task'`), the completed one carrying the qualifier in `filter: { status: 'completed' }` — keyed by a CHILD field and the option VALUE, never the label `已完成`; dropped, the field counts every task and shows a plausible wrong total. `completion_rate` is a `formula` over the two summaries, authored after them (it computes only once they do). If `project` rows already exist, says the recompute runs only on a child write, so the backfill is `os migrate summary-nulls --apply` — not editing a task to trigger it.

evals.prompt: 工单需要一个「负责人」，每个客服只能看到自己负责的工单。
evals.expected_output: Adds NO owner lookup: every object already carries the platform `owner_id` (reassignable, stamped to the creator), which is what owner-scoped visibility and "my records" views read — a hand-added 负责人 lookup is a second owner those never see. Sets `sharingModel: 'private'` on `ticket` (owner-only by default) and leaves `ownership` at its default. A people field is added only for a role DISTINCT from the owner (a reviewer, an approver), as `type: 'user'`.

evals.prompt: 新建「供应商」对象：公司名称、联系邮箱、合作状态（合作中 / 已终止）。
evals.expected_output: `supplier` with `label: '供应商'` and Chinese field and option labels (`公司名称`, `联系邮箱`, `合作状态`; options `active` → `合作中`, `terminated` → `已终止`) — labels follow the language of the request, only machine names stay ASCII `snake_case`. An authored `sharingModel`, `pluralLabel` and `icon`; the status is a `select` with a non-empty `options` list.
